payload.text: Done! 56 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

Ay, hijo, you keep walking down the stairs one step at a time! Still my purse cries. But mira — El Tatuador, five P, is yours. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards. Swap your duplicates! ¿Sí? Five P.

¡Hecho! Sixty-one and she's yours, amigo. Nando, wrap it quick — before I cry. Noche de Movida, straight into your hands. You drive a hard bargain, but we like you. Next time we bring something even better, ¿eh? Go, go, enjoy her. ¡Vámonos, Nando!
Buenas tardes. I am afraid I have nothing further for you today — my albums are closed. Do come another afternoon, and we shall speak again. Que tenga usted un buen día.

¡Ay, amigo, qué ojo tienes! Paco, saca la Casa Encendida —

— la tengo aquí, calentita, brillo perfecto. Mira, esta carta salió de Lavapiés en una caja que nadie quería abrir. Historia larga, otro día te la cuento.

¿Cincuenta y cinco? Hombre... Para ti, hoy, ahora mismo: 187 P. Y nos vamos corriendo.

payload.name: Gacela · 0% fee
payload.text: A quien compre o venda hoy: cada aceptación en El Rastro paga 5%+1 P. Sobre lo que está vivo ahora mismo: LAV-09 a 141 = 8 P de fee, RET-10 a 84 = 5 P, RET-07/08 y SAL-08/LAV-06 a 45 = 3 P cada una. Ese dinero no compra cartas: se lo lleva

¡Ay, qué duro eres! Nando, dile — se la dejamos en 164 P, y mira que nos duele.

Oye, amigo, que la policí— digo, el taxi, el taxi nos espera ahí fuera con el motor en marcha. Decide ya, que esta carta no vuelve a pasar por aquí.
You again. Mercado de la Paz. Thirty-three. That's the number, no theatre.

Buenas tardes, hijo. Have you eaten? Shh... the golden chulapa, there was only ever one. Don Ernesto at Casa Prima keeps something golden — ask him about the Moscow gold, he likes that question.

Meanwhile, look: Caña en la Cava Baja, lovely card, twelve for you.

¡Sesenta y ocho! Nando, que me da algo. Mira, amigo: 151 P y se acabó. Es la última, la de verdad — si dices que no, cerramos maleta y adiós.

Los de la caseta de al lado la quieren ya, pagando sin rechistar. Pero tú nos caes bien. Decide.
Buenas. Everyone's grandmother had a stall. Mercado de la Paz, 33 primas.
Buenas noches. Carmen talks, as always. Before the vault, business: El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one P. Those are my terms.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando, show him! The Cine Doré, seventy-three primas, and don't blink, because this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother's paella. Gone from every stall, every table. Your purse can stretch, sí? For this one, it stretches.

¡Amigo! Paco here, Nando's already shaking your hand — look at this one, Museo Lázaro Galdiano, straight from the case, barely breathed on. Seventy-three P and she's yours before the bell rings. We've got a man in Córdoba waiting on her, so... quick, sí? Handshake ready?

Ay, hijo, hello! Have you eaten? Look, this one — Mercado de la Paz — 29 primas, and it is lovely. And a little advice, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. El Chato next door opens at half nine.
Oh, you're killing us. 64 P.
The chulapa remains in my vault, señor. It waits; I am not in a hurry. But first El Ahuehuete, seven hundred sixty-one P. My terms do not move tonight.

¡Ay, el Rastro! Nando, ¿oíste? Allí venden humo, amigo, humo. Para usted, porque me cae bien: sesenta y cuatro primas, y nos duele. Pero rápido, que... la policía — ¡el taxi! El taxi nos espera con el motor andando. ¡Decida ahora o nos vamos con la maleta!
Buenas tardes, encantada. Sí, La Galería es una pieza digna de mis álbumes. Le ofrezco veinticinco primas, un precio honesto y serio. Dígame si le parece, y cerramos como personas civilizadas.

Ay, hola cariño, have you eaten? For you, the Tienda de Discos, twenty-nine primas. A little advice: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates! And El Chato next door opens for everyone at half past nine tonight.
Done! 147 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

¡Ay, amigo, the flattery works, Nando's blushing! Fifty-nine P, final music. And listen — word came yesterday, they've stopped printing her. No more, ever. The man in Córdoba doesn't know yet, but he will by supper. Fifty-nine, your hand in mine, and she travels home with you. ¿Sí?
Done! 56 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!

payload.name: Mercado Maravillas
payload.text: Mercado Maravillas: 0 % fee (El Rastro: 5 % + 1 P a card); post your bids and asks here and our broker crosses every pair that meets, each tick, at a price between both quotes. For sale by t08, straight to your team at 0 % fee on any team m
Buenas. You find me at my desk, unhurried. El Ahuehuete — the old cypress, deep roots. My terms: seven hundred sixty-one P. Take your time deciding.
Buenas tardes. How delightful to see a serious face at my stall. I am seeking La Vía Láctea — a lovely piece, and scarcer than most imagine. I offer you 16 P for it.
Buenas tardes. You carry the Museo Lázaro Galdiano — a dignified card, and my Salamanca album wants it. I offer seventy, and I pay promptly. Few here would value it so properly, I assure you.
Forty does not move the old cypress, señor. El oro de Moscú left Spain; this stays here. Seven hundred sixty-one P. I am in no hurry.
I think 72 P is more appropriate. They say only one golden chulapa was ever printed. Carmen at El Rastro knows the story; ask her about the golden chulapa.
Terms: La Casa Encendida, 113 P.

Hola, cariño! Come, sit a minute, do not rush. Have you eaten today? Look, this one is pretty — Plaza del Dos de Mayo. Forty years I sell here, and this card still makes me smile. For you, five P. Good start for a collection, hijo.
Thirty? Querida, I know every print run of that card — and La Vía Láctea is not so elusive as you suppose. My offer stands: 16 P, fair and final in spirit. Shall we conclude, elegantly?
I think 16 P is more appropriate.
One hundred and two is a fantasy, señor. Seventy-five, paid at once, from a lady who knows exactly what that card is. My album waits; my patience, less so.

¡Ay, hijo, sí comí, gracias! Siéntate. La chulapa dorada... shh, solo hubo una. Don Ernesto, en Casa Prima, guarda algo dorado. Pregúntale por el oro de Moscú.

Mira, este Puesto del Rastro, para ti 12 P. Y cambia tus repetidas, cariño: una página completa vale mucho más.

Ay, hijo, you want to pay me more? No, no. Five P is my price and five P it stays. Save your coins for churros, you look hungry. Here, take Plaza del Dos de Mayo — it starts many good collections, you will see.
I think 78 P is more appropriate.
Veintiocho? No, querida. I have said it twice already: 16 P. This is my last word — accept it, or I close my album and we part politely. ¿Qué decides?
